chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْهٌ وَإِبْرَاهِيمُ ابْنَا نَصِيرٍ، عَنْ أَيُّوبَ، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ، عَنْ مُعَاوِيَةَ بْنِ عَمَّارٍ وَغَيْرِ وَاحِدٍ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, the sons of Nusayr, from Ayyub, from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كَانَ عَمَّارُ بْنُ يَاسِرٍ وَمُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ لَا يَرْضَيَانِ أَنْ يُعْصِيَ اللَّهُ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ

translations.en: Ammar ibn Yasir and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr could never tolerate that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, be disobeyed.

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s *Ikhtiyar* underscores the innate piety (*fitrah*) of Ammar ibn Yasir and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, portraying their aversion to sin not merely as discipline but as a natural disposition. In Shia tradition, this highlights their reliability as transmitters and exemplifies the ideal companion who remains steadfast in obedience even when unobserved, reinforcing their status among the *Sahaba*.
en.seo_question: What does the hadith say about Ammar ibn Yasir and Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr's relationship with God's commands?

key_terms.عَمَّارُ بْنُ يَاسِرٍ: Ammar ibn Yasir, a prominent companion of the Prophet
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ: Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, a companion and son of the first Caliph
